title.rendered: 10 Most FAQ’s About Hair Loss and LLLT

content.rendered:
Hair loss is one of the most heartbreaking events in life that we all encounter at some point. The journey that starts with hair thinning leads to hair fall, and eventually hair loss. However, hair loss is reversible; you can stop, revoke, and control the damage with the help of hair loss treatments, procedures, and advanced technology. Hair loss is a universal problem. Many of us search for the causes and treatments for hair loss online. In this post, we have gathered 10 Most FAQ’s about hair loss and LLLT. 

FAQs About Hair and LLLT for Hair Loss

Q1. How many stages are there in hair growth?

The growth cycle of hair involves three stages –anagen, catagen, and telogen. Anagen is the phase where hair growth takes place. It lasts anywhere between three and five years. Hairs then enter the catagen stage; it is the transitional stage where hair follicles begin to break down and prepare to grow new hair. The last stage or the resting phase is telogen; in this stage, hair follicles grow new hair and push the old hair strands to fall out. 

For more information about in depth details about the hair growth cycle, read The Hair Growth Cycle.

Q2. I see hair on my pillow, comb, and even in the bathtub. Is it a sign of hair loss?

Well, it is important to know that losing hair is natural; shedding is part of the hair cycle growth. A healthy person with thicker and healthier hair also loses anywhere between 50 and 100 hairs a day. Our scalp has more than 100,000 hair follicles that continuously go through different stages, i.e., growth, shed, and rest. So, if you are losing 50-100 hair every day, then it is natural.

However, if the hair loss is more frequent or severe, it’s time to take some action. For example, if you start losing hair in clumps or notice thinning start to take place on areas of the scalp, it is time to start looking into some treatment options that can help combat your condition.

Q3. What is the most common form of hair loss in men?

While hair loss is a universal problem, men tend to lose more hair compared to their female counterparts. With growing age, men become more susceptible to hair loss. By the age of 35, most men experience hair loss to some extent. Some even begin to lose hair in their teen years or early 20s. 

Many reasons account for hair loss among men, but the leading cause is androgenic alopecia. It is a medical term for male pattern baldness, a hereditary hair loss condition. You are more likely to experience male pattern baldness if you have a family history or genetic disposition. Men with androgenic alopecia lose hair at the temples and crown in an M-shaped pattern. 

Q4. Is my hairstyle causing me to lose hair?

We all love to style our hair in different ways; your hairstyle reflects your personality. While some hairstyles look cool and trendy, they may cause you to lose hair, leading to traction alopecia. Traction alopecia is a form of hair loss in a small area on the scalp. Tight hairstyles that involve persistent pulling or use of force on hair roots are the leading cause of traction alopecia. For instance, if you braid your hair tightly, it can cause hair to fall out. It is best to choose those styles that put less strain on your hair follicles. 

Q5. I have heard a lot about LLLT for hair loss.  How does it work?

Low Level Light Therapy (LLLT) is a groundbreaking technology for hair loss victims. Pattern hair loss causes your hair to become thinner and lighter with each growth cycle. At one point, hair follicles become miniaturized. LLLT uses light or laser energy below a specific threshold and wavelength. LLLT enhances the cellular respiration, which helps to grow back thicker and fuller hair. It absorbs the dead cells and energizes aging cells. 

Q6. Is it safe to use LLLT if I am under 18?

LLLT uses a cold or soft laser that produces no heat. So, it does not burn or injure the skin. Both men and women ages 18 and up can use laser therapy to help regrow their hair. However, if you are questioning this treatment, aways make sure to consult your physician. 

Q7. What is the difference between the laser and the light devices used for hair loss?

The main difference is the power and energy output. Some devices cover only a specific area of the scalp. Other devices require people to manually comb or brush the hair for 15 to 30 minutes. Thus, it does not provide a consistent application of light on the scalp. Kiierr’s laser hat hair growth system is a completely automated, hands-free, and easy to use device. It covers the scalp and provides consistent light.  You only have to wear the laser cap every other day for 30-minutes and the cap automatically turns off after the treatment time is up. 

Q8. When will I see the results of LLLT?

Hair loss is progressive; you will experience more hair loss over time if you don’t seek treatment. Depending on the state and type of hair loss, you should see tiny hair growth in six to twelve months.  For maintaining the hair quality, you should continue the LLLT sessions once or twice per week.

Q9. How is Kiierr’s laser cap different from other LLLT treatments?

The first-ever FDA-approved LLLT device had 9 laser diodes; it is a hand-held comb that the user must use for 15 minutes twice a week. Another FDA-cleared device for hair loss is an in-office hood with 90 bulbs; the user must sit under the hood twice a week. Kiierr’s laser cap for hair growth provides a more user-friendly and time-efficient solution. It has 272 medical grade laser diodes that cover the scalp fully. In addition, Kiierr’s laser cap is a portable, hands-free device. This means you can complete your treatment whenever and wherever is convenient for you. 

Q10. Why should I prefer Kiierr rather than receiving an in-office LLLT session?

The Kiierr272 Premium Hair Growth System is designed for at-home use. It eliminates the need to spend time and money on visiting clinics. The cap uses 272 diodes and cold lasers that provide extensive coverage to the scalp. All you have to do is wear the laser cap for 30-minutes every day while doing your routine work. It offers the same result and output as most in-clinic lasers with the remarkable convenience.

 

Conclusion

Hair loss is not fun! But, with these 10 most FAQ about hair loss, hopefully you got some of your questions answered. If you still have questions that were not addressed in this article, shoot us a comment below and we can help you out!

 

For more information on hair loss and LLLT, don’t miss a chance to read this next article. Up next: Everything you need to know about LLLT.
